acceptance: Each un-gated benchmark has live differential coverage and registered compat rules
Gate rules remain for every benchmark not yet validated
One PR per benchmark, each opened with make pr-open
context:
Item-specific guardrails: never lift a gate without live differential coverage. Never lift several gates in one PR.

Shared Exasol guardrails: worktree-only writes with make agent-write-preflight; explicit-path staging, never git add -A; commit identity check, no attribution trailers; uv only; lazy pyexasol import; no credentials in Git, logs, fixtures, or tracker; no live cloud runs; code-skill self-review then make pr-preflight and make pr-open, no auto-merge without make pr-ready; durable artifacts carry no tracker IDs or session narrative; stop and report on failed gates, unverified behavior, license questions, or unapproved host changes.
description:
The adapter core blocks every benchmark except TPC-H and TPC-DS, because Exasol's upper-case identifier folding, empty-string-as-NULL, missing types (TIME, BLOB, UUID, arrays, JSON), and reserved words may silently change other benchmarks' answers. Lift the gate one benchmark at a time, starting with SSB, then read_primitives, then ClickBench (mixed-case columns, large data).

Tasks, per benchmark:
1. Translate its DDL and queries to exasol; check reserved-word collisions against sqlglot's list and a live EXA_SQL_KEYWORDS query; check column types.
2. Add live differential coverage against DuckDB at the smallest scale.
3. Register any needed rewrites or skips in sql_compat with reasons.
4. Remove only that benchmark's gate rule and update docs/platforms/exasol.md.

Decision gates:
- G1 Start only with explicit user priority. One benchmark per PR.
- G2 If a benchmark's data contains meaningful empty strings (distinct from NULL), stop and decide with the user whether to keep it gated.
- G3 If a benchmark needs an unsupported type, keep it gated and record the reason in the rule.
